title: Experiment 1 — Effect of Heat (Temperature) on a Chemical Equilibrium System
apparatus: Equipment: Bunsen burner or hot plate, test tubes, test tube holder, test tube rack, thermometer, goggles · Chemicals: Copper(II) sulphate pentahydrate or cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate and distilled water
description: Demonstrate the reversible effect of heat (temperature) on a chemical equilibrium system using hydrated copper(II) sulphate (CuSO₄·5H₂O) or cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate (CoCl₂·6H₂O).

title: Experiment 2 — Measure the pH of Different Solutions Using pH Paper
apparatus: Equipment: Beakers, pH paper, pH scale, watch glass, stirrer · Chemicals: Baking soda, HCl, soap solution, curd, garden soil, table salt, caustic soda, vinegar, lemon juice, apple juice, orange juice and oxalic acid
description: Measure the pH of household and laboratory solutions using universal indicator pH paper and classify them as acidic, neutral, or basic.

title: Experiment 3 — Standardise the Given Solution of Sodium Hydroxide Volumetrically
apparatus: Equipment: Burette, iron stand, funnel, clamp, pipette, beakers, conical flasks, dropper · Chemicals: Sodium hydroxide solution, standard solution of hydrochloric acid, phenolphthalein
description: Standardise the given sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution volumetrically by acid-base titration against a standard hydrochloric acid (HCl) solution using phenolphthalein indicator.

title: Experiment 4 — Measure the Exact Molarity of a Solution of Oxalic Acid Volumetrically
apparatus: Equipment: Burette, iron stand, funnel, clamp, pipette, beakers, conical flasks, dropper · Chemicals: Standard solution of NaOH, oxalic acid solution, phenolphthalein
description: Determine the exact molarity of a given oxalic acid ((COOH)₂·2H₂O) solution volumetrically by titrating against a standard sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution.

title: Experiment 5 — Silver Nitrate Test to Detect Chloride (Cl⁻), Bromide (Br⁻), and Iodide (I⁻) Ions
apparatus: Equipment: Test-tube, test-tube stand, stirrer · Chemicals: NaI, NaBr, NaCl, AgNO₃, and NH₄OH
description: Perform the silver nitrate (AgNO₃) precipitation and ammonium hydroxide (NH₄OH) solubility test to detect and distinguish chloride (Cl⁻), bromide (Br⁻), and iodide (I⁻) halide ions.

title: Experiment 6 — Flame Test to Detect Calcium, Strontium, Barium, and Copper Ions
apparatus: Equipment: Platinum wire / glass rod, match box, watch glass, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp · Chemicals: Salt of each ion: calcium (Ca²⁺), strontium (Sr²⁺), barium (Ba²⁺), and copper (Cu²⁺) and concentrated HCl
description: Perform a flame test to detect the presence of calcium (brick-red), strontium (crimson-red), barium (apple-green), and copper (bluish-green) ions by observing their characteristic flame colours.

title: Experiment 7 — Sodium Nitroprusside Test to Detect Ketones
apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp, match box, dropper, water bath · Chemicals: Fructose solution, distilled water, sodium nitroprusside solid and sodium hydroxide solution
description: Perform the alkaline sodium nitroprusside test to detect the presence of a ketone functional group (formation of a wine-red colouration).

title: Experiment 8 — Fehling’s and Tollens’ Tests to Detect Aldehydes
apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp, match box, water bath, dropper · Chemicals: Formaldehyde, Tollens’ reagent, Fehling’s solution and glucose solution
description: Perform Fehling’s test (brick-red Cu₂O precipitate) and Tollens’ silver mirror test to detect the presence of an aldehyde functional group.

title: Experiment 9 — Sodium Carbonate / Bicarbonate Limewater Test to Detect Carboxylic Acids
apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, delivery tube, dropper · Chemicals: Limewater, carboxylic acid, solid sodium carbonate and distilled water
description: Perform the sodium carbonate test (with limewater confirmation of brisk CO₂ effervescence) to detect the presence of carboxylic acids.

title: Experiment 10 — Ferric Chloride (FeCl₃) Test to Detect Phenol
apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, dropper · Chemicals: Phenol solution, freshly prepared ferric chloride solution and distilled water
description: Perform the neutral ferric chloride (FeCl₃) test to detect the presence of phenol (formation of a violet/purple complex).

title: Experiment 11 — Potassium Permanganate (KMnO₄) Baeyer’s Test for Unsaturation
apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, dropper · Chemicals: Cinnamic acid solution, ghee, vegetable oil and KMnO₄ solution
description: Perform the alkaline potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) test to differentiate between saturated and unsaturated organic compounds by observing decolourisation of purple KMnO₄.

title: Experiment 12 — Demonstrate Softening of Permanent and Temporary Hard Water
apparatus: Equipment: Beaker, test tubes, china dish, funnel, iron stand, filter paper, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp · Chemicals: Water sample (beakers containing two types of hard water), lime water, small soap bar, sodium carbonate solution and sodium zeolite
description: Demonstrate the softening of temporary hard water (by boiling / Clark’s limewater method) and permanent hard water (by adding washing soda Na₂CO₃ or passing through sodium zeolite).
